title: North Kerala & the Malabar Coast: Athirappilly, Wayanad, Kannur and Bekal in 8 Days
meta_title: North Kerala Malabar Tour 8 Days: Wayanad & Bekal
meta_description: 8-day North Kerala tour: Athirappilly Falls, Kozhikode, Wayanad's Edakkal Caves and Banasura, Theyyam country in Kannur and Bekal Fort, ending at Mangaluru.
tagline: Kerala's quiet north: waterfalls, spice hills, Theyyam and a fort on the sea
intro: Most visitors to Kerala never go north of Kochi. This one-way route runs up the Malabar coast from Kochi airport to Mangaluru: India's widest waterfall at Athirappilly, the spice port of Kozhikode where Vasco da Gama landed, two nights in the green hills of Wayanad, the Theyyam ritual country around Kannur and the sea fort of Bekal. Drives are short, and there is no need to double back.
highlights: Athirappilly Falls, about 25 m high and the widest waterfall in Kerala
Kozhikode beach at sunset and Kappad, where Vasco da Gama landed in 1498
Edakkal Caves, with Neolithic rock carvings, and Banasura Sagar Dam in Wayanad
Muzhappilangad, a 4 km drive-in beach near Kannur
A Theyyam performance in a village shrine, in season
Bekal Fort, one of the largest forts in Kerala, on the Arabian Sea

days.title: Land in Kochi and drive to Athirappilly Falls
days.summary: Arrival at Kochi airport and transfer to Athirappilly.

rows.label: On landing · Kochi airport (COK)
rows.title: Meet your driver
rows.text: With a name sign at arrivals.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Athirappilly Falls
rows.text: The Chalakudy River drops about 25 m over a wide rock face. Walk down to the base for the full view, about 20 minutes each way.
notes: Rocks near the water are slippery. Stay behind the barriers, especially in the monsoon.

rows.label: Optional
rows.title: Vazhachal Falls
rows.text: A second cascade 5 km upstream.

days.note: Hornbills are often seen along the Vazhachal road early in the morning.

days.title: Up the coast to Kozhikode
days.summary: Drive to Kozhikode, with the beach and Mananchira Square in the evening.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Drive north
rows.text: Via Thrissur, where you can stop at the Vadakkunnathan temple from outside.
notes: Most Kerala temples admit Hindus only. Men remove shirts inside, women wear saree or salwar.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Kozhikode beach and Mananchira Square
rows.text: Sunset at the old lighthouse, then the square and its large temple tank.
notes: Kozhikode is famous for halwa on SM Street (Mittai Theruvu) and banana chips fried in coconut oil.

days.note: Kozhikode cooking is mostly non-vegetarian. We book a vegetarian restaurant for you in advance.

days.title: Kappad beach and up the ghat to Wayanad
days.summary: Kappad beach, then the Thamarassery ghat road to Wayanad with the Lakkidi viewpoint.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Kappad beach
rows.text: A stone pillar marks where Vasco da Gama landed in 1498.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Thamarassery ghat and Lakkidi viewpoint
rows.text: Nine hairpin bends up to the Wayanad plateau. The Chain Tree is a short stop by the road.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Check in at your plantation resort
rows.text: Coffee, pepper and cardamom estates around the resort.

days.note: Weekend traffic on the ghat can add an hour. We leave Kozhikode by 10:00.

days.title: Edakkal Caves, Banasura Sagar and Pookode Lake
days.summary: Full day of sightseeing in Wayanad.
strip: Climb about 1 km to the caves

rows.label: About 09:00
rows.title: Edakkal Caves
rows.text: Rock shelters on Ambukuthi Mala with carvings thousands of years old. A steep path and steps, about 45 minutes up.
notes: Open about 09:00 to 16:00 and closed on Mondays. Daily visitor numbers are capped, so arrive early.
Not suitable for people with knee or heart problems.

rows.label: Optional · Ambalavayal
rows.title: Wayanad Heritage Museum
rows.text: Tribal tools, weapons and stone carvings, 10 minutes from Edakkal.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Banasura Sagar Dam
rows.text: India's largest earth dam, with speedboat rides among small islands.

rows.label: Late afternoon
rows.title: Pookode Lake
rows.text: A natural freshwater lake in the forest with pedal boats, near your resort.

days.note: Soochipara (Sentinel Rock) Falls is in the Meppadi area, affected by the 2024 landslides. We check whether it is open before we offer it.

days.title: Down to Kannur and the drive-in beach
days.summary: Drive to Kannur via Muzhappilangad beach.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Down the Periya ghat
rows.text: Through coffee estates to the coast.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Muzhappilangad drive-in beach
rows.text: A 4 km firm sand beach where cars can drive along the waterline.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Theyyam (seasonal)
rows.text: From about November to May, village shrines around Kannur stage Theyyam, a ritual dance in which the performer becomes the deity. We find the night's performance for you.
notes: This is worship, not a show. Dress modestly, stay at the edge and do not use flash.

days.note: Theyyam often starts late at night and runs till dawn. One or two hours is plenty.

days.title: North to Bekal
days.summary: Drive to Bekal and check in to your beach resort.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: St Angelo Fort, Kannur
rows.text: A Portuguese fort from 1505 on the sea.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Arrive Bekal
rows.text: Check in and relax by the sea.

days.note: Bekal's resorts are on the Kappil and Pallikere beaches, quieter than any in south Kerala.

days.title: Bekal Fort and Kappil beach
days.summary: Bekal Fort, Kappil beach and an optional Valiyaparamba backwater cruise.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Bekal Fort
rows.text: A keyhole-shaped laterite fort of about 1650 with an observation tower over the sea.
notes: Go before 10:00 for softer light and fewer people.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Kappil beach
rows.text: Palm groves and a quiet beach.

rows.label: Optional
rows.title: Valiyaparamba backwaters
rows.text: A houseboat or country-boat cruise on North Kerala's largest backwater, about 30 km away.

days.note: Swim only where the resort says it is safe. The Arabian Sea has strong currents from May to September.

days.title: Bekal to Mangaluru airport
days.summary: Transfer to Mangaluru airport for your flight.
strip: About 70 km, 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours

rows.label: After breakfast
rows.title: Drive to Mangaluru (IXE)
rows.text: Into Karnataka on the coastal highway.

days.note: Mangaluru also has trains to Mumbai and Goa if you would rather go by rail.

hotel.name: Hand-picked resorts at each stop
hotel.area: Athirappilly, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Bekal
hotel.about: Rainforest lodges at Athirappilly, plantation resorts in Wayanad and beach resorts at Bekal. Premium options include Taj Bekal and Vythiri Village in Wayanad.

included: 7 nights in the resorts listed or similar
Private air-conditioned car from Kochi to Mangaluru
excluded: Entry fees, boating and cave tickets
best_time: October to March: dry, green and about 22° to 32°. Theyyam season runs from about November to May. The monsoon (June to September) is lush but rough at sea, and ghat roads see landslides.
seasons: Dry and pleasant, about 22° to 32°; cool nights in Wayanad.
Hot and humid on the coast, about 34°; Theyyam continues.
Heavy rain, waterfalls at full flow, beaches closed for swimming.

faqs.q: Why does the tour end in Mangaluru, not Kochi?
faqs.a: Bekal is about 70 km from Mangaluru but over 350 km from Kochi. Flying home from Mangaluru saves a full day of driving.
Yes, from about November to May. Performances follow the temple calendar, so we confirm the nearest one a few days before.

faqs.q: Is Wayanad safe after the 2024 landslides?
faqs.a: The landslides struck the Mundakkai and Chooralmala area. The rest of Wayanad, including Kalpetta, Vythiri, Edakkal and Banasura, is open. We avoid hill areas after very heavy rain.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

price_note: Contact us for a personalised quote for your dates, flights and hotel choice.
entry: Aadhaar, passport, driving licence or voter ID for flights, trains and hotel check-in
Tourist e-Visa applied online before travel
Most ASI monuments sell tickets online and by UPI at the gate
About INR 20 to 50 for Indians, more for foreigners
entry_notes: Carry the original photo ID, not a photocopy. Security at airports and many temples checks it.
Phone and internet: Jio and Airtel work best across most of this route. Download offline Google Maps before hill or forest stretches, where signal drops.

good_to_know.title: UPI, cards and cash
good_to_know.text: UPI works almost everywhere, even at small stalls. Keep some cash in INR 100 and 200 notes for temples, parking, tips and places where the network is weak.

good_to_know.title: Temple and shrine etiquette
good_to_know.text: Cover shoulders and knees. Remove shoes where asked, and carry socks for hot stone floors. Leather belts and bags are not allowed inside some Jain and Hindu temples. Ask before photographing people and inside shrines.

good_to_know.title: Water and street food
good_to_know.text: Drink sealed bottled or filtered water only. Choose busy stalls where food is cooked in front of you, and skip cut fruit and ice from roadside stalls.

good_to_know.title: Driving times
good_to_know.text: Indian roads are slower than the kilometres suggest: plan on 40 to 50 km an hour on highways and much less in hills and towns. Your driver's breaks and meal stops are built into the timings.

good_to_know.title: Plugs and tipping
good_to_know.text: Plugs are Indian three-pin and two-pin, 230 volts. Tipping drivers and guides about INR 300 to 500 a day is appreciated.

dining_intro: India is the easiest country in the world for vegetarian and Jain travellers. We send your dietary brief to every hotel, and your driver knows clean, pure-vegetarian restaurants on each road day.
dining_avoid: Ask for food cooked fresh and tell the kitchen clearly if you eat Jain: no onion, garlic, ginger, potato or other root vegetables. Many dishes start with an onion-garlic base even when the menu says vegetarian.
food_card: Hum shuddh shakahari (Jain) hain. Pyaz, lahsun, adrak, aloo, gajar ya koi bhi zameen ke neeche ki sabzi nahi. Ande nahi. Kripya taaza banaiye. Dhanyavaad.
